# 2 Kings Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 228r–228v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_007_page_001.jpg, 2KI_007_page_002.jpg

---

**7:1** And-said Elisha: Hear [shim'u] the-word of-YHWH. Thus says YHWH: About-this-time tomorrow [ka-et machar], a-seah [se'ah] of-fine-flour [solet] for-a-sheqel, and-two-seahs of-barley [se'orim] for-a-sheqel, in-the-gate of-Shomron.

**7:2** And-answered the-officer [ha-shalish] on whose-hand the-king was-leaning [nish'an] the-man of-God and-said: Behold, [if] YHWH made windows [arubbot] in-the-heavens [ba-shamayim], could-this thing be [ha-yihyeh ha-davar ha-zeh]? And-he-said: Behold, you [are] seeing [ro'eh] with-your-eyes, but from-there you-shall-not eat.

**7:3** And-four men, lepers [metsor'aim], were at-the-entrance [petach] of-the-gate. And-they-said each to-his-neighbor [re'ehu]: Why are-we sitting [yoshevim] here until we-die?

**7:4** If we-say: Let-us-enter the-city — and-the-famine [is] in-the-city — and-we-shall-die there. And-if we-sit here, we-shall-die. And-now, come [lekhu] and-let-us-fall [venipplah] to the-camp of-Aram. If they-spare-us [yechayunu], we-shall-live, and-if they-kill-us, we-shall-die.

**7:5** And-they-rose in-the-twilight [ba-neshef] to-go to the-camp of-Aram. And-they-came to the-edge [qetseh] of-the-camp of-Aram, and-behold, no-man [eyn ish] [was] there.

**7:6** For the-Lord [Adonay] had-caused the-camp of-Aram to-hear a-sound [qol] of-chariots [rekhev] and-a-sound of-horses [sus] — a-sound of-a-great army [chayil gadol]. And-they-said each to-his-brother: Behold, the-king of-Yisra'el has-hired against-us the-kings of-the-Hittites [malkhey ha-Chittim] and-the-kings of-Mitsrayim [Egypt] to-come against-us.

**7:7** And-they-rose and-fled in-the-twilight and-left their-tents and-their-horses and-their-donkeys — the-camp as-it-was [ka-asher hi] — and-fled for-their-lives [nafesham].

**7:8** And-came these lepers [ha-metsor'aim ha-elleh] to the-edge of-the-camp and-entered one tent and-ate and-drank and-carried from-there silver and-gold and-garments and-went and-hid [vayatminu]. And-they-returned and-entered another tent and-carried from-there and-went and-hid.

**7:9** And-they-said each to-his-neighbor: We [are] not doing right [lo khen anachnu osim]. This day [is] a-day of-good-news [besorah], and-we [are] keeping-silent [machshim]. If-we-wait until-the-light of-the-morning [or ha-boqer], punishment [avon] will-find-us. And-now, come, let-us-go and-tell the-house of-the-king.

**7:10** And-they-came and-called to the-gatekeeper [sho'er] of-the-city and-told them, saying: We-came to the-camp of-Aram, and-behold, no-man [eyn ish] and-no-sound [eyn qol] of-a-man [adam], but the-horses tied [asurot] and-the-donkeys tied, and-the-tents as-they-were [ka-asher hennah].

**7:11** And-he-called the-gatekeepers [ha-sho'arim] and-they-told the-house of-the-king inside [penimah].

**7:12** And-arose the-king [in] the-night and-said to-his-servants: Let-me-tell-you, please [aggidah na], what Aram has-done to-us. They-know that we [are] hungry [re'evim], and-they-went-out from the-camp to-hide [lehechave'] in-the-field, saying: When-they-come-out from the-city, we-shall-seize-them alive [chayyim] and-into the-city we-shall-enter.

**7:13** And-answered one of-his-servants and-said: Let-them-take, please, five of the-horses that-remain [ha-nish'arim], which remain in-it — behold, they [are] like-all the-multitude [hamon] of-Yisra'el that remain in-it; behold, they [are] like-all the-multitude of-Yisra'el that have-perished [tammu] — and-let-us-send and-see.

**7:14** And-they-took two chariot-horses [rekhev susim], and-sent the-king after the-camp of-Aram, saying: Go and-see.

**7:15** And-they-went after-them to the-Yarden, and-behold, all the-way [ha-derekh] [was] full of-garments and-vessels [kelim] which Aram had-cast-away [hishliku] in-their-haste [behechafezam]. And-returned the-messengers and-told the-king.

**7:16** And-went-out the-people and-plundered [vayavozu] the-camp of-Aram. And-a-seah of-fine-flour was for-a-sheqel, and-two-seahs of-barley for-a-sheqel, according-to-the-word of-YHWH.

**7:17** And-the-king had-appointed the-officer on whose-hand he-was-leaning [over] the-gate, and-the-people trampled-him [vayirmesuhu] in-the-gate, and-he-died, as the-man of-God had-spoken, who spoke when-the-king came-down to-him.

**7:18** And-it-was as the-man of-God had-spoken to the-king, saying: Two-seahs of-barley for-a-sheqel and-a-seah of-fine-flour for-a-sheqel shall-be about-this-time tomorrow in-the-gate of-Shomron.

**7:19** And-answered the-officer the-man of-God and-said: And-behold, YHWH [is] making windows in-the-heavens — could-this thing be? And-he-said: Behold, you [are] seeing with-your-eyes, but from-there you-shall-not eat.

**7:20** And-so it-was to-him, and-the-people trampled-him in-the-gate, and-he-died.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — seah of fine flour for a sheqel:** This prophecy specifies exact market prices — an astonishing reversal from the famine prices of 6:25. The gate was the marketplace. Elisha announces economic restoration with the precision of a commodity trader.

**v.2 — windows in the heavens:** The officer's skepticism uses the image of *arubbot* (windows/lattices) in heaven — echoing Genesis 7:11 (the flood) and Malachi 3:10. His disbelief is answered by a devastating irony: he will see the fulfillment but not participate in it.

**v.6 — kings of the Hittites and kings of Egypt:** The Arameans fear a coalition. "Kings of the Hittites" (*malkhey ha-Chittim*) refers to the Neo-Hittite city-states of northern Syria. The divine sound creates panic from phantoms — YHWH wins without a single Israelite soldier.

**v.9 — day of good news (besorah):** The Hebrew *besorah* is the word that later becomes "gospel" (via Greek *euangelion*). The lepers — social outcasts living at the margin — become the first bearers of good news. Their moral awakening ("we are not doing right") is the chapter's ethical center.

*— EMET*
